description: Protocol catalog — declarative config for all contextual intelligence protocols

explainTemplates.title: Back-to-back fatigue risk
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Team on zero rest: expect ~3% shooting efficiency drop, ~1.5 more turnovers, reduced minutes efficiency.

userSummary.risk_averse: This team is playing on zero rest. Back-to-back games are one of the strongest predictors of underperformance. Consider avoiding.
userSummary.aggressive: Short rest creates variance. If you're betting the other side, there's an edge here.
userSummary.novice: One of these teams played last night too. Tired teams make more mistakes and miss more shots.
userSummary.expert: B2B schedule spot: historical efficiency delta -3.2% 3PT, +1.5 TOV/game. Factor into player props and totals.

explainTemplates.title: Travel and altitude stress
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Cross-country travel or altitude exposure creates measurable fatigue and conditioning disadvantage.

userSummary.risk_averse: Long travel or altitude change adds hidden fatigue. Teams visiting Denver especially struggle with conditioning.
userSummary.aggressive: Travel fatigue is baked into some lines but not all. Look for mispriced visitor spreads.
userSummary.novice: When teams fly across the country or play at high altitude, they tend to get tired faster.
userSummary.expert: Travel delta: >1500mi cross-country + altitude >5000ft historically shows ~8% home advantage boost.

explainTemplates.title: Pace mismatch volatility
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Large pace differential creates scoring variance. Totals become structurally unstable.

userSummary.risk_averse: These teams play at very different speeds. That makes scoring unpredictable — totals bets are risky.
userSummary.aggressive: Pace mismatch = mispriced totals. If you like volatility, this is your game.
userSummary.novice: One team plays fast and the other plays slow. This makes it hard to predict the final score.
userSummary.expert: Pace delta >6 poss/game: over/under pricing carries elevated variance. Consider alt lines or halves.

explainTemplates.title: Defensive matchup vulnerability
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Significant defensive rating gap or key defender absence creates scoring opportunity spike.

userSummary.risk_averse: One side has a clear defensive advantage. Bets on the weaker defense carry extra risk.
userSummary.aggressive: Defensive gap means scoring opportunities. Player props on the offensive side could be undervalued.
userSummary.novice: One team is much better at defense. The weaker team might give up a lot of points.
userSummary.expert: Defensive rating differential >6pts/100poss creates exploitable scoring asymmetry. Check opponent paint usage.

explainTemplates.title: Pace collapse risk
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Both teams play slow with strong defense. Playoff-style games amplify this. Totals bets become dangerous.

userSummary.risk_averse: Both teams are likely to slow this game down. Over bets are especially risky.
userSummary.aggressive: If you see value in the under, the defensive profiles support it. But it's a grind game — low ceiling for props.
userSummary.novice: Both teams like to play slow, tough defense. Don't expect a high-scoring game.
userSummary.expert: Dual slow-pace + sub-108 DRtg: historical pace collapse frequency ~35% in these matchups. Unders with caution.

explainTemplates.title: Foul trouble risk
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Referee crew calls significantly more fouls than average. Star minutes at risk, game flow disrupted.

userSummary.risk_averse: This referee crew is whistle-happy. Star players could get in foul trouble and see reduced minutes.
userSummary.aggressive: High-foul refs mean more free throws and game stoppages. Consider the over if both teams attack the paint.
userSummary.novice: The referees tonight call a lot of fouls. Star players might sit out more than usual.
userSummary.expert: Crew foul rate +3.0 above avg: star player minute volatility increases ~15%. Factor into prop minutes thresholds.

explainTemplates.title: Lineup instability
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Multiple rotation changes or new starting lineup creates chemistry uncertainty and higher variance outcomes.

userSummary.risk_averse: This team has significant lineup changes. New combinations mean unpredictable chemistry — higher risk.
userSummary.aggressive: Lineup chaos creates mispricing. If the market hasn't adjusted to the new rotation, there's an edge.
userSummary.novice: This team changed their lineup a lot recently. New player combinations don't always work well together.
userSummary.expert: 3+ lineup changes with starter out: correlation tags shift, prop baselines unreliable. Structural variance elevated.

explainTemplates.title: Injury shadow effect
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Star returning on restricted minutes or key player absence creates mispricing in props and team lines.

userSummary.risk_averse: A key player is injured or on restricted minutes. The odds may not fully reflect this — be careful with related bets.
userSummary.aggressive: Injury-related mispricing is one of the best edges in sports betting. Look for value on the replacement players.
userSummary.novice: An important player is hurt or limited. This changes how well the team can play.
userSummary.expert: Star on minutes restriction: market overvalues presence vs actual impact. Check prop lines for deflated alternatives.

explainTemplates.title: Revenge game motivation
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Player facing former team shows historical usage rate spike of ~3-5%. Props may be undervalued but variance increases.

userSummary.risk_averse: A player is facing their old team. They'll be extra motivated, but emotional play can go either way.
userSummary.aggressive: Revenge games are real. Usage spikes of 3-5% are well-documented. Look at the over on their props.
userSummary.novice: A player is going up against the team that traded them. They usually try extra hard in these games.
userSummary.expert: Revenge narrative: +3-5% USG% historical, but sample size warning. Value in points/assists over, fade rebounds.

explainTemplates.title: Momentum and streaks
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Extended streaks create regression risk (wins) or morale uncertainty (losses). Not blindly directional.

userSummary.risk_averse: Long streaks often end. Whether winning or losing, the pattern is unlikely to continue forever.
userSummary.aggressive: Streaks are noise until they aren't. The market overreacts to both hot and cold teams — find the disconnect.
userSummary.novice: This team has been winning (or losing) a lot lately. Streaks can change at any time.
userSummary.expert: Win streak >5: regression probability ~62% next game. Loss streak >5: bounce-back rate ~55%. Context-dependent.

explainTemplates.title: Sharp money detection
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Line moved against public betting percentages. Professional bettors see something the market hasn't priced in.

userSummary.risk_averse: Professional bettors are betting the opposite of the public. That's usually a warning sign.
userSummary.aggressive: Sharp money is the strongest market signal. When pros disagree with the public, follow the money.
userSummary.novice: The betting line moved in the opposite direction of what most people are betting. Smart money might know something.
userSummary.expert: Reverse line movement: >2pt against >65% public action. Steam move probability high. CLV tracking recommended.

explainTemplates.title: Bookmaker trap line
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Line moving toward heavy public side. Books are comfortable with the exposure — potential trap.

userSummary.risk_averse: The line is making the popular bet look even better. That's suspicious — bookmakers rarely lose.
userSummary.aggressive: Classic trap setup. If 70%+ of the public is on one side and the line keeps moving their way, fade the public.
userSummary.novice: The odds keep moving to make the popular pick look better. But the bookmakers might be setting a trap.
userSummary.expert: Trap line pattern: >70% public + line movement toward public side. Historical public side win rate ~42% in this pattern.

explainTemplates.title: Officiating bias pattern
explainTemplates.analystSummary: Referee crew shows historical bias in home advantage. Spread bets should account for officiating tendencies.

userSummary.risk_averse: This referee crew tends to favor the home team. If you're betting on the visitor, factor in an extra disadvantage.
userSummary.aggressive: Ref tendencies are underpriced. If the crew historically gives home teams +2 points, that's not in the spread.
userSummary.novice: Some referee crews tend to make calls that help the home team more than others.
userSummary.expert: Crew home advantage delta: +2.0pts historical. Adjust spread expectation accordingly. Granular crew data available.
